hug-1-1-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-1-001.title: Population density in four districts
hug-1-1-001.description: Hypothetical equal-area districts: NW 80, NE 20, SW 80, SE 20 people per square kilometer. North is up. Values are density, not population counts.
hug-1-1-001.caption: Each district covers 100 km². The grid shows geographic adjacency, not real countries.

hug-1-1-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-1-002.title: Residents in a hypothetical region
hug-1-1-002.description: One dot represents 1,000 residents. Twelve dots cluster in the northwest; three lie in the southeast. The center has no plotted dots. No elevation or roads are shown.
hug-1-1-002.caption: Dots represent approximate population locations within the hypothetical region.

hug-1-1-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-1-003.title: Two hypothetical elevation slopes
hug-1-1-003.description: Uniform-scale elevation contours. West: 100 m at x=10, 200 m at x=20, 300 m at x=30. East: 100 m at x=55, 200 m at x=75, 300 m at x=95. Contours run north–south. Each successive line differs by 100 m.
hug-1-1-003.caption: Hypothetical straight contours; compare average eastward gradients between the 100 m and 300 m lines.
hug-1-1-003.unitLabel: Elevation isolines: meters above a common datum; interval 100 m

hug-1-1-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-1-004.title: Three hypothetical towns
hug-1-1-004.description: North-up reference map with a uniform scale of 2 km per coordinate unit. A is at (20,15), B at (80,15), C at (20,45). B lies directly east of A; C is south of A. No roads are shown.
hug-1-1-004.caption: Straight-line map geometry only. The scale bar represents 40 km.

hug-1-2-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-2-001.title: Field inventory records
hug-1-2-001.description: Hypothetical records combine an interview description, a passenger tally, a station identifier and a measured location. Each record retains its collection method.
hug-1-2-001.caption: The phrase is one participant’s account, not a representative citywide estimate.

hug-1-2-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-2-002.title: Eligible residents and app participants
hug-1-2-002.description: Hypothetical residents aged 15 and older: ages 15–24 have 1,000 residents and 600 app users; ages 25–64 have 2,000 residents and 1,200 app users; ages 65+ have 1,000 residents and 100 app users. Counts represent people, not trips.
hug-1-2-002.caption: Resident counts come from a complete hypothetical census; app participation is voluntary. Children younger than 15 are outside this dataset.

hug-1-2-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-2-003.title: Usable satellite-image coverage
hug-1-2-003.description: Hypothetical equal-area districts with cloud-free usable optical pixels: NW 80%, NE 95%, SW 10%, SE 15%. This is the percentage observed clearly, not a measurement of land-cover type.
hug-1-2-003.caption: One collection date; no replacement images or observations of obscured pixels are supplied.

hug-1-2-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-2-004.title: Traffic observation metadata
hug-1-2-004.description: Hypothetical Street A: weekday 07:00–09:00, 360 vehicles/hour. Street B: Sunday 13:00–15:00, 160 vehicles/hour. Both use observers counting vehicles crossing a fixed point, but collection schedules differ.
hug-1-2-004.caption: Each rate summarizes only its stated observation window; neither is an all-week average.

hug-1-3-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-3-001.title: Candidate clinic sites
hug-1-3-001.description: Hypothetical accessibility estimates: R costs 90 units and newly serves 3000 residents; S costs 120 and serves 4000; T costs 70 and serves 2500; U costs 80 and serves 2000. Existing access is excluded from the newly served counts.
hug-1-3-001.caption: One site may be funded. Fixed budget: at most 100 units. All other eligibility conditions are assumed equal.

hug-1-3-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-3-002.title: Schools and mapped floodplain
hug-1-3-002.description: Hypothetical north-up map. The middle polygon, x 35–65, is the mapped floodplain. A at (20,15) enrolls 1000; B at (50,15) enrolls 300; C at (80,45) enrolls 500. West and East polygons lie outside the supplied floodplain.
hug-1-3-002.caption: Numbers at school points are enrollments. The boundary is a hypothetical screening layer, not a forecast of certain flooding.
hug-1-3-002.unitLabel: School locations (enrollment) over mapped floodplain boundary

hug-1-3-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-3-003.title: Two hypothetical census counts
hug-1-3-003.description: Area A: earlier 4000, later 6000 residents. B: earlier 1000, later 2000. C: earlier 2000, later 2200. Both counts use unchanged area boundaries and the same resident definition.
hug-1-3-003.caption: Two observed dates, not forecasts. These counts alone do not measure every type of service need.

hug-1-3-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-3-004.title: District temperature comparison
hug-1-3-004.description: Hypothetical matched observation windows: district R received tree planting and changed from 34°C before to 31°C after; district S received no planting and changed from 32°C to 29°C. Districts were not randomly assigned.
hug-1-3-004.caption: Comparable measurement procedures and time windows; other environmental and social changes were not controlled.

hug-1-4-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-4-001.title: Business locations in a study area
hug-1-4-001.description: Hypothetical north-up schematic. Five businesses occupy coordinates (20,15),(35,15),(50,15),(65,15),(80,15) on a common local coordinate grid. No road or river is shown.
hug-1-4-001.caption: Each dot is one business. The diagram encodes positions, not business size or the cause of the pattern.

hug-1-4-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-4-002.title: Two connections to one employment center
hug-1-4-002.description: Hypothetical towns P and Q: P is 20 km from the center in straight-line distance and the listed journey takes 50 minutes; Q is 45 km away and takes 25 minutes.
hug-1-4-002.caption: Journey times use the same observation period; compare the listed trips, not an unobserved future service.

hug-1-4-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-4-003.title: Visiting share by distance band
hug-1-4-003.description: Hypothetical groups of 100 residents each, represented at 5,15 and 25 km from one recreation center:60%,30% and 10%, respectively, made at least one visit in the same month.
hug-1-4-003.caption: Equal-sized groups, one observation period. Other differences between the groups were not controlled.

hug-1-4-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-4-004.title: Transit stops and shops by district
hug-1-4-004.description: Hypothetical districts L,M,N have respectively 0,5,10 transit stops and 4,20,40 shops in the same observation year.
hug-1-4-004.caption: District-level counts only; no causal experiment or historical sequence is provided.

hug-1-5-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-5-001.title: Aquifer recharge and withdrawal
hug-1-5-001.description: Hypothetical aquifer: annual recharge is 100 million m³, current annual withdrawal is 90 million m³ and proposed annual withdrawal is 140 million m³. The initial volume stored is unspecified.
hug-1-5-001.caption: Use the proposed scenario. Assume no other inflows or outflows and unchanged annual rates.

hug-1-5-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-5-002.title: Land-cover inventories in one district
hug-1-5-002.description: Hypothetical fixed 100 km² district: earlier forest 70, cropland 20, built-up 10 km²; later forest 40, cropland 30, built-up 30 km². Categories are exhaustive and mutually exclusive.
hug-1-5-002.caption: Both inventories use the same boundary and categories; individual parcel transitions are not supplied.

hug-1-5-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-5-003.title: Paved cover and a river connection
hug-1-5-003.description: Hypothetical north-up map: West has 80% paved cover and East has 20%. A river arrow runs from the western area toward the eastern area. These are land-cover percentages, not flood probabilities.
hug-1-5-003.caption: Arrow shows river direction only. No discharge or building-level flood-depth estimates are given.
hug-1-5-003.unitLabel: Paved surface (% of each area); arrow = river direction

hug-1-5-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-5-004.title: Two farming responses in similar settings
hug-1-5-004.description: Hypothetical areas A and B each receive 500 mm annual rain and have similar soils and terrain. A has irrigation access and grows vegetables; B lacks irrigation access and grows drought-tolerant grains.
hug-1-5-004.caption: A deliberately simplified comparison. Crop systems are observed choices, not universal outcomes for these conditions.

hug-1-6-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-6-001.title: Household connections within one country
hug-1-6-001.description: Hypothetical country divided into four districts with equal household counts. Connection rates are NW 90%, NE 70%, SW 10% and SE 30%. The national rate is 50%.
hug-1-6-001.caption: The denominator is households in each district. Each district contains the same number of households.

hug-1-6-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-6-002.title: Service access in a two-country region
hug-1-6-002.description: Hypothetical region containing only countries E and F: E has 900 residents, of whom 810 have the service; F has 100 residents, of whom 10 have the service.
hug-1-6-002.caption: All residents in the region are counted once. The same service definition and observation date apply in both countries.

hug-1-6-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-6-003.title: Different groupings of unchanged local data
hug-1-6-003.description: Hypothetical equal-population local areas A and B each have 80% access, C and D each have 20%. Grouping I: Zone 1=A+B, Zone 2=C+D. Grouping II: Zone 1=A+C, Zone 2=B+D. Resulting rates are 80%,20% and 50%,50%.
hug-1-6-003.caption: Membership changes between grouping plans, not residents’ access. Every local area is included once in each plan.

hug-1-6-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-6-004.title: National and listed-city housing medians
hug-1-6-004.description: Hypothetical monthly rent medians in the same currency and year: Country A national 600, listed city 1200; Country B national 800, listed city 1000.
hug-1-6-004.caption: National and city medians summarize different populations. City population sizes and individual rent distributions are not supplied.

hug-1-7-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-7-001.title: Language L household shares
hug-1-7-001.description: Hypothetical north-up map: households using Language L at home are NW 70%, NE 60%, SW 55%, SE 30%. These are district shares, not a claim that all households use the same language.
hug-1-7-001.caption: Regional inclusion rule: at least 60% of households. Exact threshold values qualify; household language use need not be exclusive.

hug-1-7-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-7-002.title: Clinic service connections
hug-1-7-002.description: Hypothetical service diagram: Town A sends 300 recorded trips to the Clinic and Town B sends 150 recorded trips to the same Clinic during one observation period. Arrowheads point toward the Clinic.
hug-1-7-002.caption: Counts represent trips, not unique residents. Positions are schematic; no legal boundary or complete service-area edge is drawn.
hug-1-7-002.assumptions: Only the displayed service links are represented. Participation is based on observed trips; no claim of equal population, shared culture or a precise outer boundary.

hug-1-7-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-7-003.title: Residents’ inclusion of areas in Old Town
hug-1-7-003.description: Hypothetical survey of 100 residents for each area: A is included by 90 respondents, B by 55 and C by 20. Each respondent answers yes or no for the relevant area.
hug-1-7-003.caption: Responses describe regional perceptions, not legal jurisdiction. Samples are equal in size and are not claimed to represent every resident.

hug-1-7-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-1-7-004.title: Two regional criteria applied to three areas
hug-1-7-004.description: Hypothetical area A has 900 mm annual rain and 40% of recorded trips bound for the central city. B has 900 mm and 80%; C has 400 mm and 80%.
hug-1-7-004.caption: Wet criterion: rain at least 800 mm. Functional criterion: more than 50% of trips to the central city. The two attributes are measured separately.

hug-2-1-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-1-001.title: Population and land in Area P
hug-2-1-001.description: Hypothetical Area P has 120000 residents, 600 km² of total land, 100 km² of arable land and 5000 farmers. Farmers are a subset of residents.
hug-2-1-001.caption: All areas use km². Agricultural density uses the number of farmers divided by arable land area.

hug-2-1-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-1-002.title: Equal populations with different land bases
hug-2-1-002.description: Hypothetical Country A has 400000 residents, 2000 km² total land and 100 km² arable land. Country B has 400000 residents, 1000 km² total land and 400 km² arable land.
hug-2-1-002.caption: Population and land refer to the same observation year; arable land is part of total land in each country.

hug-2-1-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-1-003.title: Settlement near a river corridor
hug-2-1-003.description: Hypothetical north-up schematic: sixteen equal-value population dots lie within six horizontal coordinate units of a river at x=50 in a study area extending from x=0 to100. No employment or political layer is shown.
hug-2-1-003.caption: Each dot represents the same number of residents; dots show a schematic distribution, not exact household positions.

hug-2-1-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-1-004.title: Employment and settlement in two towns
hug-2-1-004.description: Hypothetical P and Q share similar climate, terrain and water access. P: earlier 100 industrial jobs and 2000 residents, later 1000 jobs and 8000 residents. Q: 100 jobs and 2000 residents at both dates.
hug-2-1-004.caption: Jobs and residents are separate counts. The paired observations are not a controlled experiment or individual employment histories.

hug-2-2-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-2-001.title: Clinic journeys in two settlement patterns
hug-2-2-001.description: Hypothetical areas Dispersed and Compact each have 10000 residents and one clinic offering comparable services. Mean one-way clinic journey: Dispersed 35 minutes; Compact 5 minutes.
hug-2-2-001.caption: Mean travel time measures journeys, not waiting time or medical quality. Clinic-to-population ratios are the same.

hug-2-2-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-2-002.title: Transport energy across settlement patterns
hug-2-2-002.description: Hypothetical annual transport energy per resident: Low density 12000 units, Medium density 8000, High density 4000. The same measurement procedure is used; populations and other impacts are not supplied.
hug-2-2-002.caption: A comparison of per-resident use, not a controlled experiment. Other differences in infrastructure and travel behavior were not controlled.

hug-2-2-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-2-003.title: Residents in four assembly districts
hug-2-2-003.description: Hypothetical equal-area districts: NW and NE each have 1000 residents; SW and SE each have 4000. Every district elects exactly one representative under the stated rule.
hug-2-2-003.caption: These are resident counts, not density values or a description of any real country’s electoral law.

hug-2-2-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-2-004.title: Population, land and resource demand
hug-2-2-004.description: Hypothetical Area A: 1000 residents, 100 km² total land, annual demand 100 units per resident. Area B: 10000 residents, 100 km² land, annual demand 10 units per resident.
hug-2-2-004.caption: The demand measure uses the same resource unit and year in both areas; all residents are included once.

hug-2-3-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-3-001.title: Age-sex composition of Population R
hug-2-3-001.description: Hypothetical Population R. The accompanying table supplies male and female shares for every cohort. Both sides use one common percentage scale and whole-population denominator; oldest ages appear at the top.
hug-2-3-001.caption: Each bar is a percentage of the entire population, not a percentage within one sex. Cohorts below 80 are ten-year groups; 80+ is open-ended. All shares sum to 100%.

hug-2-3-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-3-002.title: Age-sex composition of Population S
hug-2-3-002.description: Hypothetical Population S. Male and female cohort shares use the same whole-population denominator and are provided in the data table. Causes of the pattern are not supplied.
hug-2-3-002.caption: Each bar is a percentage of the entire population, not a percentage within one sex. Cohorts below 80 are ten-year groups; 80+ is open-ended. All shares sum to 100%.

hug-2-3-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-3-003.title: Age groups for a dependency comparison
hug-2-3-003.description: Hypothetical population: 3000 residents aged 0–14, 6000 aged 15–64 and 1000 aged 65+. Groups are mutually exclusive and cover the entire population.
hug-2-3-003.caption: These are age groups, not observed employment or financial-support categories.

hug-2-3-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-3-004.title: Age-sex composition of Population T
hug-2-3-004.description: Hypothetical Population T. The full male/female percentage table accompanies the graph. Recorded ages describe population composition, not identical personal needs, employment or exact life expectancy.
hug-2-3-004.caption: Each bar is a percentage of the entire population, not a percentage within one sex. Cohorts below 80 are ten-year groups; 80+ is open-ended. All shares sum to 100%.

hug-2-4-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-4-001.title: Annual population-accounting observations
hug-2-4-001.description: Hypothetical midyear population 100000. During the year: 2200 births, 800 deaths, 1500 immigrants and 2500 emigrants. The four flow counts use the same population boundary.
hug-2-4-001.caption: Midyear population is the rate denominator. It is not identified as the beginning-of-year population.

hug-2-4-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-4-002.title: Paired crude rates over three periods
hug-2-4-002.description: Hypothetical crude birth/death rates per 1000 residents: Early 35/15, Middle 28/8, Later 18/8. Birth and death rates in each pair use a common population denominator.
hug-2-4-002.caption: Natural increase excludes migration. These observations do not establish that future rates will remain fixed.

hug-2-4-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-4-003.title: Assumed positive annual growth rates
hug-2-4-003.description: Hypothetical populations X and Y have annual total growth rates of 2% and 1%, respectively. For this projection exercise the rates are assumed to remain constant.
hug-2-4-003.caption: Use the approximate rule of 70 divided by the percentage growth rate; real populations need not retain a constant rate.

hug-2-4-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-4-004.title: Annual migration between two areas
hug-2-4-004.description: Hypothetical north-up map: an arrow from A to B represents 3000 movers and a reverse arrow from B to A represents 500. No other migration is recorded for these areas in this exercise; births and deaths are not shown.
hug-2-4-004.caption: Numbers label annual movers in the arrow direction, not population totals or all components of change.
hug-2-4-004.unitLabel: Movers per year; arrowhead marks destination

hug-2-5-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-5-001.title: Four classical transition stages — schematic
hug-2-5-001.description: Original hypothetical model: birth/death rates per 1000 are Stage 1 42/40, Stage 2 40/15, Stage 3 25/9 and Stage 4 10/10. A solid line with circles marks births; a dashed line with squares marks deaths.
hug-2-5-001.caption: Connected markers summarize four classical stages, not equal-duration years or an actual country. Ignore migration for natural increase; real rates can fluctuate and pathways vary.

hug-2-5-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-5-002.title: Different rate levels and growth gaps
hug-2-5-002.description: Hypothetical crude birth/death rates per 1000 residents: A 40/39, B 38/12, C 22/8, D 10/9. These are one-time observations using consistent definitions.
hug-2-5-002.caption: Compare both rate levels and their differences. A snapshot does not provide a complete historical transition record.

hug-2-5-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-5-003.title: Fertility variation within one country
hug-2-5-003.description: Hypothetical district total fertility estimates: NW 4.2, NE 1.6, SW 3.8, SE 1.4 births per woman under the specified age-specific fertility schedule. Mortality, migration and earlier observations are not supplied.
hug-2-5-003.caption: Color classes summarize fertility only; they are not transition-stage thresholds. No real-country statistics are used.

hug-2-5-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-5-004.title: Changing composition of recorded deaths
hug-2-5-004.description: Hypothetical Earlier period: infectious 800, chronic 200, total 1000 deaths. Later period: infectious 100, chronic 300, total 400. Both periods cover equal lengths and a population of 100000.
hug-2-5-004.caption: The two cause groups are mutually exclusive and exhaustive in this simplified exercise. Counts describe populations, not individual diagnoses.

hug-2-6-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-6-001.title: Contrasting assumed growth processes
hug-2-6-001.description: Hypothetical food-unit demand at steps0–3:2,4,8,16 million; supply:4,6,8,10 million. Solid circles show demand; dashed squares show supply.
hug-2-6-001.caption: Original stylized projection, not real observations. Demand is one food unit per resident. Equal conceptual steps use a doubling of demand and a fixed supply increment; no innovation or trade is assumed.

hug-2-6-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-6-002.title: Productivity on a fixed cultivated area
hug-2-6-002.description: Hypothetical earlier period:100 hectares,10 food units/hectare,1000 units harvest,1000 residents. Later:100 hectares,20 units/hectare,2000 harvest,1500 residents.
hug-2-6-002.caption: Synthetic observations with comparable harvest periods. Total harvest equals cultivated area times yield. No claim about future rates or production costs is supplied.

hug-2-6-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-6-003.title: Food availability and district populations
hug-2-6-003.description: Two hypothetical districts: West1000 residents with2 available food units per resident; East500 residents with0.2. Circle areas, not radii, encode available food per resident.
hug-2-6-003.caption: West:1000 residents; East:500. Each person requires1 unit for this period. No transfers between districts. Circle areas are proportional to food per resident, not population. Schematic boundaries are not to scale.
hug-2-6-003.unitLabel: Circle area = available food units per resident

hug-2-6-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-6-004.title: Changing rather than constant demand growth
hug-2-6-004.description: Hypothetical demand at steps0–3:10,12,13,13 food units; supply:12,14,16,18. Demand is one unit per resident, with all quantities expressed in the same unit.
hug-2-6-004.caption: Original hypothetical observations. Constant per-person demand makes changes in demand reflect population-related demand; these are not a forecast or a universal demographic path.

hug-2-7-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-7-001.title: Three policy instruments and their stated aims
hug-2-7-001.description: Hypothetical policies A–C. The statements describe intentions, not measured effects.
hug-2-7-001.caption: Original policy scenarios; no actual country’s laws are represented. Classification depends on each stated aim and mechanism.

hug-2-7-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-7-002.title: Fertility trends with and without a package
hug-2-7-002.description: Hypothetical P fertility values3,2.8,2.4; Q3,2.7,2.3 births per woman. A fertility-support package began only in P after the first observation.
hug-2-7-002.caption: Equal observation intervals. Observational data only; regions were not randomly assigned and other changes are not controlled. No exact causal effect can be read from the lines alone.

hug-2-7-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-7-003.title: Access under uniform subsidy eligibility
hug-2-7-003.description: Hypothetical eligible households within30 minutes of a participating childcare center:NW80%,NE70%,SW30%,SE20%. Eligibility rules are the same nationally.
hug-2-7-003.caption: Access percentages do not give household totals or observed fertility effects. Districts are schematic, not real places.

hug-2-7-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-7-004.title: Age composition of planned admissions
hug-2-7-004.description: Hypothetical plan A admissions:ages0–14 100,15–64 800,65+100. Plan B:100,1800,100. Values are people, not percentages or employed-worker counts.
hug-2-7-004.caption: All admitted people fall into these three mutually exclusive age groups. Working age does not establish employment. Original scenarios, not real-country plans.

hug-2-8-001.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-8-001.title: Education and adolescent birth rates
hug-2-8-001.description: Hypothetical districts A,B,C have women’s secondary completion30%,60%,90% and adolescent birth rates80,50,20 per1000 girls ages15–19 per year.
hug-2-8-001.caption: Comparable one-time district observations. No individual records, adolescent population totals or controls for other influences are supplied.

hug-2-8-002.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-8-002.title: Sex composition by migration scope
hug-2-8-002.description: Hypothetical internal migration:600 women,400 men. International migration:200 women,300 men. Each person appears in one category during the observation period.
hug-2-8-002.caption: Original sample; counts do not establish causes or a universal migration rule. Internal means within the country, international means across its border.

hug-2-8-003.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-8-003.title: Paid work and unpaid care time
hug-2-8-003.description: Hypothetical daily averages among sampled working-age adults: women4 paid hours and6 unpaid care hours; men8 paid and2 unpaid. Categories do not overlap.
hug-2-8-003.caption: Original sample averages, not every individual’s schedule. No wages, preferences or causes of time allocation are provided.

hug-2-8-004.attribution: Original PrepAtlas schematic and synthetic data
hug-2-8-004.title: Maternal-death counts with equal birth totals
hug-2-8-004.description: Hypothetical maternal deaths:Earlier80,Later30. Each comparable period records10000 live births. No particular intervention is assigned by the data.
hug-2-8-004.caption: Counts use a consistent maternal-death definition. Compute ratios using live births; this is not an all-population mortality rate or medical advice.
